_doc: must = indicator ids that have to fire on the emulator; mustnot = must not fire. Checked by check.py.

frida_server.note: frida-server only (renamed fs64, not attached). /proc/net/tcp is SELinux-blocked for apps on Android 10+, so FRIDA_PORT is expected to be blind on API 30+.

frida_attach.note: Real Frida 17 agent injected by frida-server into the app process (memfd:frida-agent-64.so, gum-js-loop/gmain/gdbus threads).

magisk.note: Magisk (rootAVD) default config: Zygisk off, DenyList off. Must catch Magisk across the Java (pkg/bins), mount (tmpfs + module bind) and native-syscall (su via SYS_newfstatat) layers.

frida_hook.note: Frida agent attached AND an Interceptor hook placed on libc open() — the inline-hook check must see the patched prologue.

magisk_zygisk.note: Magisk with Zygisk enabled, app NOT on the DenyList. NOTE: on the google_apis x86_64 (arm64-translation) image Zygisk does not load (native-bridge conflict), so this currently equals plain Magisk — runtime hiding is NOT exercised yet; the AOSP 'default' image is where Zygisk activates.

magisk_zygisk_denylist.note: Magisk + Zygisk + DenyList enforced for this app — what survives Magisk's own hiding. The DenyList unmounts Magisk's own bind-mounts in the app's namespace and hides the app from the manager, but it cannot hide the su binary from a raw SYS_newfstatat syscall (native_su_bin) or the module bind-mounts left in mountinfo (mount_module_bind); those are the must-fire proof that hidden Magisk is still caught. NOTE: on the google_apis x86_64 (arm64-translation) image Zygisk does not load (native-bridge conflict), so DenyList is not truly active here — full hiding is exercised only on an image where Zygisk loads (AOSP 'default') or on a real device.
